title: Fix: add ALTER TABLE migration for recipes.slug + drink_recipes.slug
description:
## Why
Production deploy on dietpi is broken: \"no such column: recipes.slug\" / \"no such column: drink_recipes.slug\" from every recipe-listing query.

## Root cause
Commit 9d46bed (\"refactor: simplify slugs to pre-release form\") added the \`slug\` column to \`recipes\` and \`drink_recipes\` by editing the existing \`m20260118_000002_create_recipes\` and \`m20260213_000010_create_drink_recipes\` migrations IN-PLACE, rather than adding a new ALTER TABLE migration. SeaORM tracks already-run migrations by name, so existing DBs (like dietpi's) skip the modified migrations and never gain the column. New code queries the missing column and 500s.

## What's needed
New migration \`m20260424_000012_add_recipe_slugs\`:
1. \`ALTER TABLE recipes ADD COLUMN slug TEXT\` (nullable initially)
2. \`ALTER TABLE drink_recipes ADD COLUMN slug TEXT\` (nullable initially)
3. Backfill: iterate existing rows, compute \`slugify(name)\`, dedupe collisions by appending \`-2\`, \`-3\`, etc., write back
4. Create unique indexes \`idx_recipes_slug\` and \`idx_drink_recipes_slug\`
5. Skip the NOT NULL upgrade — SQLite would require the create-copy-drop-rename dance, and the app always populates slug. Existing fresh DBs already have NOT NULL; this drift is acceptable.

## Verification
- \`cargo test\` green
- Migration applies cleanly on a snapshot of the pre-slug schema
- Migration is no-op on a fresh DB (column already exists from the edited create migration — guard with a column-exists check, or use \`if not exists\` on the indexes)
- Deploy to dietpi via \`just deploy dietpi@dietpi.local\`, verify Recipes tab loads
close_reason: Implemented as new migration m20260424_000012_backfill_recipe_slugs. Idempotent across legacy + fresh DBs via has_column gate. Tests cover backfill, collision dedup, fallback, idempotency, uniqueness. Pushed in 38c01aa. Awaiting deploy verification on dietpi.

title: MCP server rejects non-localhost Host headers — blocks LAN deploy
description:
Connecting to the deployed MCP endpoint at http://dietpi.local:3000/mcp from another machine fails with HTTP 403:

    Forbidden: Host header is not allowed

The rejection comes from rmcp's StreamableHttpService, which ships with a DNS-rebinding-protection allowlist defaulting to ["localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1"] (rmcp-1.4.0 src/transport/streamable_http_server/tower.rs:72). server/src/mcp/mod.rs:100 builds the service with StreamableHttpServerConfig::default(), inheriting that localhost-only allowlist. Any LAN hostname (dietpi.local, IP) gets a 403.

This breaks the README's own LAN-deploy story — the threat model at mcp/mod.rs:18-23 explicitly accepts LAN-side trust, but the host allowlist hadn't been widened to match.

## Fix

Make the allowlist configurable via MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS env var (comma-separated). Merge with — not replace — the rmcp localhost defaults so dev mode never breaks. Empty/unset env var = current behavior.

Tests:
- env var unset → defaults preserved
- env var set with extra hosts → hosts appended, defaults still present
- ports handled per rmcp semantics (entry without port matches any port)

After deploy: set MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS=dietpi.local on the dietpi box's systemd unit / launcher.

## Why P1
Holding up release — without it Claude Desktop can't connect to the deployed server at all.
close_reason: Closed

title: Document MCP threat model: LAN-only, name-is-not-a-credential, any-authed-user-is-admin
description:
The MCP server uses family-member display name as the bearer token (Authorization: Bearer Alice). This is a deliberate 'household trust' design, but the security posture relies entirely on the operator firewalling the port — and that requirement is not documented anywhere reachable by an admin who doesn't read source.

**Three structural facts that need explicit documentation:**

1. /mcp is LAN-only by design. The server binds 0.0.0.0 (server/src/main.rs:64). Operator MUST firewall the port or place behind a reverse proxy with real auth before exposing the host beyond the LAN.

2. Authentication is identity selection, not a secret. Names appear in list_people, get_family_overview, shopping briefs, and meal plans. They are not credentials.

3. Any authenticated family member can read and write any data. There is no per-user authorization. AuthenticatedPerson is plumbed through but only whoami reads it.

**Where to put it:**
- README.md — short note in MCP section
- server/src/mcp/mod.rs — top-of-file doc comment with the same content (so contributors see it before extending the surface)

**Out of scope for this bead:** replacing the auth scheme (tracked separately). Goal here is to make the threat model explicit so the release ships honest about its security posture.
close_reason: Closed

title: Migration: add or_alternative pass-through to frozen Ingredient structs in m13/m14/m15
description:
The three new backfill migrations each redefine an Ingredient struct (per the 'migrations are frozen-in-time' rule in CLAUDE.md). The runtime IngredientDto got an or_alternative field in fewd-4nb, but the frozen migration structs do not.

**Failure mode:** If any of these migrations re-runs against a DB that has or_alternative populated (CI fresh-DB with seeded data, future re-seed scenario, restore-without-seaql_migrations recovery), the field is silently dropped on the JSON round-trip.

**Files:**
- server/migration/src/m20260427_000013_split_ingredient_name_and_prep.rs:78-91
- server/migration/src/m20260428_000014_reparse_misbucketed_ingredients.rs:101-114
- server/migration/src/m20260429_000015_peel_size_parens_from_ingredient_name.rs:79-92

**Fix (trivial, additive):** add to each frozen struct:

```rust
#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
or_alternative: Option<serde_json::Value>,
```

Pass-through Value matches m13's existing pattern for the amount field. Not a re-edit of shipped logic — just a new field added to a struct, which is safe per the migration discipline rules.

Doesn't impact dietpi (migrations already ran there), but blocks any fresh deploy / DB recovery scenario from being safe.
close_reason: Closed

title: Frontend: or_alternative silently dropped in CookingView, AdaptRecipePanel, AiSuggestionSection
description:

- src/components/AiSuggestionSection.tsx:409-415 (AI suggestion card)

**Fix:** Replace each inline <li> body with <IngredientLineText ingredient={ing} />. Same swap that's already in place in RecipeDetail, DrinkRecipeDetail, RecipeMatchCard, and the AI results list in CocktailSuggester.

The fewd-9az tests live on IngredientLineText itself, so they don't catch consumers that bypass it. Companion follow-up bead will add integration-level tests asserting or_alternative renders through these three components.

title: Bump vite past path-traversal advisory (5.x → 6.4.2+ or 7.x)
description:
## Why
Open dependabot advisory: \"Vite Vulnerable to Path Traversal in Optimized Deps \`.map\` Handling\" (medium). Vulnerable range is `<= 6.4.1`, so our current vite 5.4.21 is affected. `bun update` cannot move us — package.json pins vite to `^5.0.8` and the fix only exists on later majors.

## What's needed
Major bump with coordinated peer bumps:
- `vite` 5.4.21 → 7.x (latest stable; 6.x is patched at 6.4.2+ but already EOL trajectory)
- `@vitejs/plugin-react` 4.x → 5.x (peer-locked to vite major)
- `vitest` 1.6.x → 3.x (peer-locked to vite major)
- `@vitest/ui` matching vitest major
- Verify `vite.config.ts` and `vitest.config.ts` still compile
- Verify dev server (`bun run dev:full`) still proxies `/api` correctly
- Verify production build + `just deploy` (arm64 build) still works

## Risks
- vite 7 dropped Node 18 support; CI + local dev must be on Node 20+
- vitest 3 has reporter / API changes — some test setup may need tweaks
- jsdom 28 → 29 may be pulled along by vitest peer constraints

## Scope decision
Land as one PR: vite + plugin-react + vitest + ui must move together. Splitting adds churn without isolating risk.

## Verification
- `bun run build` clean
- `bun run test` green (currently 295 pass)
- `bun run lint` clean
- Manual smoke test of dev server + a deploy via `just deploy dietpi@dietpi.local`
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove hardcoded family PII from seed_data.rs
description:
server/src/services/seed_data.rs hardcodes the project owner's family — four first names (Steve, Amanda, Vivienne, Cleo) plus birthdates — into the default seed that runs on first DB init. This was tolerable while the repo was effectively private, but it's now visible in the public repo (and was flagged tangentially by Copilot during PR #9 review of the unrelated bd memory).

The seed is called from db.rs line 17 (seed_if_empty) only when the People table is empty, so changing the values won't disturb existing installs.

Options:
1. Replace the hardcoded list with placeholder/example names ('Alex', 'Jordan', 'Sam', 'Pat') and generic birthdates (e.g. all 1990-01-01). Lowest friction; new installs get a working empty-but-not-empty starter.
2. Drop seed_if_empty entirely so a fresh install presents a real empty state, and rely on the family-add UI to onboard. Cleaner long-term; requires confirming the rest of the app handles a People table with zero rows gracefully (MealPlanner, suggestion flows, etc.).
3. Keep seed for local dev only — gate seed_if_empty behind a SEED_DEMO_DATA env var or debug build cfg.

My recommendation: option 1 for the immediate PII removal, then option 2 as a separate cleanup if/when the empty-state UX is ready.

Acceptance criteria:
- No real names or birthdates in version-controlled seed code.
- Existing installations are unaffected (seed only runs when People is empty).
- A fresh install still produces a usable app (either via placeholder seed or via verified empty-state handling).

Files to touch:
- server/src/services/seed_data.rs (the data)
- Possibly server/src/db.rs (if option 2 or 3)

title: Harden CI workflows: ubuntu runners, rust-cache@v2, pinned bun, frozen-lockfile, least-privilege perms
description:
Harden the GitHub Actions CI workflows for cost, reproducibility, and least-privilege. All of these edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (and one touches `auto-format.yml`), so they ship as one coherent PR. Sourced from an external CI audit (2026-06-30); each item assessed against the actual workflow before logging.

Checklist:

1. **`macos-latest` → `ubuntu-latest`** on all jobs (rust-checks, frontend-checks, typos-check, all-checks) in `ci.yml`, plus the `auto-format` job in `auto-format.yml`. macOS runners bill at ~10x the minutes multiplier and CI has no host-arch dependency (deploy is cross-compiled aarch64; `cargo test` runs on the host with no parity requirement). **GOTCHA:** the `typos-check` job uses `brew install typos-cli`, which is not available on ubuntu by default — swap to the official typos install action (`taiki-e/install-action@v2` with `tool: typos-cli`) or `cargo install typos-cli`. This is the one non-mechanical part of the OS switch.

2. **Replace the hand-rolled 3-part `actions/cache@v4` blocks** (cargo registry / cargo index / `server/target`) with `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`. The current cache keys only on `hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock')` with no `restore-keys`, and caches the entire `server/target` under an immutable key — so it never refreshes within a lockfile and bloats over time. rust-cache cleans stale artifacts, keys on toolchain+lockfile, and adds restore fallbacks. Note rust-cache expects to run after the toolchain is set up (it already is, via dtolnay/rust-toolchain) and works from a workspace subdir — set `workspaces: "server"` since the crate lives in `server/`.

3. **`oven-sh/setup-bun@v1` → `@v2`** and pin `bun-version` to an explicit version instead of `latest`. `latest` makes CI non-reproducible — a bun release can break CI with zero code change.

4. **`bun install` → `bun install --frozen-lockfile`** in the frontend-checks job. Without it, CI can silently mutate `bun.lockb`, so CI isn't validating exactly what's committed. (Related: see auto-memory `project_depbump_nodemodules_branch_mismatch` — frozen-lockfile makes lockfile drift a hard CI failure, which is the desired behavior.)

5. **Add least-privilege `permissions` + `timeout-minutes`** to `ci.yml`. It currently has neither. Add a workflow-level `permissions: contents: read` (the verification jobs only read), and a per-job `timeout-minutes` (e.g. 20-30) as a runaway-minutes backstop. `auto-format.yml` already scopes `permissions: contents: write` correctly — leave it, but consider adding a timeout there too.

Verification: open the PR and confirm a full green CI run on ubuntu before merge (especially the typos install rework and that rust-cache restores/saves correctly). The migration smoke test (`scripts/migration-smoke-test.sh`) must still pass on ubuntu.
close_reason: Closed

title: systemd unit: Restart=always with no crash-loop cap -> infinite restart loop on boot panic
description: deploy/fewd.service uses Restart=always with RestartSec=5 and NO StartLimitIntervalSec/StartLimitBurst. A boot-time panic (e.g. a bad migration, or a release-only panic) makes systemd restart fewd-server every 5s forever, hammering the low-RAM dietpi box and never surfacing cleanly — the failure just loops in the journal. Sibling project chorez fixed exactly this (deploy/chorez.service): Restart=on-failure + StartLimitIntervalSec=300 + StartLimitBurst=5, i.e. ~5 quick retries to ride out a transient blip, then stop. Adopt the same pattern: switch to Restart=on-failure and add a StartLimit crash-loop cap. Observed during chorez deploy-parity comparison (read deploy/fewd.service only; not a full code review).

title: Flaky CookingView.test.tsx: lazy react-markdown findByText times out under full-suite load
description:
## Symptom

`src/components/CookingView.test.tsx` intermittently fails on `expect(await screen.findByText('Boil water.')).toBeInTheDocument()` (CookingView.test.tsx:41) with a waitFor timeout. It fails ~occasionally under the full `bun run test` suite (43 files / 378 tests running concurrently) but passes 3/3 in isolation (`bunx vitest run src/components/CookingView.test.tsx` → 11 passed). Observed twice during the fewd-2fc push: the first CI run had all 378 frontend tests green, a later run flaked this one with identical code.

## Why it flakes

The recipe steps render through a **lazy-loaded** `RecipeMarkdown` (react-markdown was code-split out of the main bundle in fewd-0fq, PR #70). The test `await`s `findByText` for content that only appears after the lazy chunk resolves. Under full-suite concurrency the dynamic import resolves slower than findByText's default 1000ms timeout, so the assertion times out before the markdown mounts. The test comment at ~line 40 already notes 'Steps render through the lazy-loaded RecipeMarkdown, so await…' — the await is there, but the timeout budget isn't generous enough under load.

## Impact

Pre-push `just ci` (the ci-before-push hook) runs the full frontend suite; a flake there refuses the push, forcing a retry. Same risk in GitHub Actions CI. It's pure test-infra flakiness — no product bug — but it taxes every push that happens to hit it.

## Fix options

1. Raise the `findByText` timeout for the lazy-markdown assertions in this test (e.g. `{ timeout: 5000 }`), matching how other lazy-loaded-component tests wait. Cheapest, targeted.
2. Mock/eagerly-resolve the lazy `RecipeMarkdown` import in this test's setup so step content renders synchronously (removes the dynamic-import timing entirely).
3. Audit for other lazy-loaded-component tests with the same default-timeout pattern (RecipeManager enhanced-view, anything using react-markdown) and apply the same remedy consistently.

## Done when

CookingView.test.tsx passes reliably under repeated full-suite runs (e.g. 10x `bun run test` with no flake), and the lazy-markdown wait pattern is robust to suite-concurrency slowdowns.
close_reason: Closed

title: Persist MCP sessions across server restart (redb- or SQLite-backed SessionManager)
description:
## Problem

MCP sessions live in-memory in rmcp's `LocalSessionManager` (`server/src/mcp/mod.rs:100`).
ANY server restart — deploy or crash — destroys every active session. The 7-day
`keep_alive` we set only prevents idle-reaping *within a running process*; it cannot
survive a restart because the state is in RAM, not persisted.

Downstream, this wedges Claude Desktop clients: after the old process exits, mcp-remote
exhausts its 2 SSE reconnect attempts and then keeps POSTing the stale `mcp-session-id`,
which the new process correctly rejects with `404 Session not found`. mcp-remote does NOT
re-`initialize` a fresh session on 404, so every tool call hangs/expires until the user
manually reconnects the connector. User-facing symptom: "Failed to call tool X" /
"request may have expired or the connection was interrupted."

## Evidence (2026-06-01 incident)

- 13:54 PDT: session established OK (old process).
- 14:11:40 PDT: `fewd-server` process restarted (deploy of the v2026-06-01 release;
  `just deploy` does `systemctl stop -> copy binary -> start`).
- 14:31 PDT onward: `get_family_overview`, `list_curated_recipes` -> `404 Session not found`
  -> `-32001 Request timed out`. Both are OLD tools — failure is transport/session level,
  not tool logic.
- Process healthy since (195 MB, stable) — single restart, not a crash loop.
- DietPi journald is volatile, so there was no log record of the restart cause — see
  separate note about `Storage=persistent`.

## Proposed direction

Implement a persistent `SessionManager` (rmcp exposes a trait in
`rmcp::transport::streamable_http_server::session`) backed by a small embedded store so
sessions survive a restart and clients reattach seamlessly.

Options to weigh during design:
- **redb** (https://www.redb.org/) — user's leaning; simple embedded KV, pure-Rust, fast.
  Adds a dependency.
- **Reuse SQLite/SeaORM** — already in the stack, zero new deps; a `mcp_sessions` table.
  Slightly more ceremony than KV.

Open questions for the investigation:
- What state does rmcp's session actually hold, and is it serializable? (protocol/init
  state, pending stream cursors). Determine whether reattach is even meaningful or whether
  we only need to recognize a known session-id and let the client resume.
- TTL / cleanup of persisted sessions (mirror the 7-day keep-alive).
- Does persisting sessions sidestep the mcp-remote "no re-init on 404" gap, or do we also
  want to file that upstream?

## Already shipped (partial mitigation, separate from this bead)

`deploy/fewd.service`: `Restart=on-failure` -> `Restart=always`. Shrinks the unreachable
window on crash/clean-exit, but does NOT preserve sessions across the restart — the real
fix is this bead.

title: MCP-token Copy button fails on LAN HTTP deploy + failure toast shows success styling
description:
The MCP-token "Copy" button fails on the dietpi (LAN HTTP) deploy, showing "Copy failed — select the text manually". Discovered 2026-06-01 right after the v2026-06-01 deploy while provisioning a token. Two distinct defects, both to be fixed properly:

## 1. Clipboard copy fails in insecure context (LAN HTTP)

`navigator.clipboard` only exists in a **secure context** (HTTPS, or `http://localhost`/`127.0.0.1`). The dietpi box serves the app over plain HTTP to a non-localhost host (e.g. `http://dietpi.local:3000`), so `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined`. `handleCopy` in `src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:369-377` therefore throws and lands in the catch. It works in `bun run dev` only because `localhost` is special-cased as secure — a classic works-on-my-machine gap that no current test catches (jsdom does not enforce secure-context rules).

**Fix:** add a legacy `document.execCommand('copy')` fallback (temporary off-screen textarea + select + copy + cleanup) gated on `navigator.clipboard && window.isSecureContext`. Use the native API when available, fall back otherwise. Keep the existing catch as a last resort for when even the fallback fails.

## 2. Failure toast renders success (green ✓) styling

`Toast` already supports `type: 'success' | 'error' | 'info'` with matching icons (`IconCheck` / `IconWarning`) in `src/components/Toast.tsx`, but defaults to `'success'`. The failure toast at `src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:375` omits the type, so a failure shows the green checkmark.

**Fix:** pass `'error'` at the copy-failure call site. **Also sweep the other failure toasts in `SettingsPanel`** that omit the type — at minimum the revoke-error toast (`SettingsPanel.tsx:363`, `Failed to revoke token: ...`) has the same bug — and pass `'error'` so genuine failures are visually honest.

## Notes

- TDD-able: mock an insecure context (`navigator.clipboard` undefined / `window.isSecureContext === false`) and assert the `execCommand` fallback path is taken; mock the secure case and assert `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is used.
- Workaround in the meantime: select the token text manually and ⌘C (the toast already instructs this).
acceptance_criteria: Copy works on the LAN HTTP (dietpi) deploy via execCommand fallback; genuine copy/revoke failures render the error (warning) toast, not the green check; test covers the insecure-context fallback path.
close_reason: Closed

title: Enhanced view offline resilience
description:
The recipe 'Enhanced view' toggle depends on a live server call and can break recipe viewing when that call fails (e.g. when offline / server unreachable).

## Reported behavior (2026-05-25)
While effectively offline (dietpi box unreachable over wifi), clicking 'Enhanced view' fired a network call that failed, after which the recipe could no longer be shown.

## Current code (main) — investigate first
`RecipeDetail` in `src/components/RecipeManager.tsx` (lines ~848-1046) actually appears to degrade gracefully today:
- `handleToggleEnhanced` calls `enhanceMutation.mutate(...)`; only `onSuccess` flips `enhancedMode`.
- Render falls back to `parsed.instructions` when `!enhancedMode || !enhancedText` (line ~1032-1038).
- On error it just shows a red error line (line ~1041-1045) and keeps the original instructions visible.

So the reported 'unviewable' behavior is likely a **deploy lag on the dietpi box** (older bundle) or a subtler bug. First step: confirm whether prod matches main; if main already degrades correctly, the resilience half may just need a redeploy + a regression test.

## How it works
- Frontend hook: `useEnhanceInstructions()` (`src/hooks/useRecipes.ts:88`) → `POST /api/recipes/:id/enhance`.
- Backend: `enhance()` in `server/src/routes/recipes.rs:154` runs an AI pass and returns instructions re-emitted with `**bold**` emphasis. `EnhancedInstructions` (RecipeManager.tsx:771-815) renders that markdown.
- So the network call *generates* the enhanced text — it is NOT purely presentational today.

## Desired outcome (preferred → fallback)
1. **Preferred — make enhanced view usable offline by persisting the enhanced text.** Cache/store the AI-enhanced instructions (e.g. a column on the recipe, generated once) so the toggle becomes a pure client-side render of already-stored data and works with no live call. Regeneration could be an explicit action.
2. **Fallback (must-have regardless) — failure must never hide the recipe.** A failed/timed-out enhance call must leave the original instructions fully viewable (confirm + add a regression test). Optionally disable/hide the toggle when offline.

## Done when
- A failed enhance call never makes a recipe unviewable (verified prod + covered by a test), and ideally the enhanced view can be toggled offline once generated.

title: Print / offline-friendly recipe view
description:
Add a way to print a recipe (or save it as a PDF) so it can be used in the kitchen without a live connection to the server.

## Motivation
Real incident (2026-05-25): wifi wouldn't route to the dietpi box; the app was only reachable over a wired CAT cable from the office. To cook a recipe in the kitchen, the user had to screenshot the recipe, open the screenshots in Preview, then unplug and carry the laptop to the kitchen. Painful workaround for a core use case (getting a recipe in front of you while cooking).

## Scope
- Add a 'Print' affordance to the recipe detail view (`RecipeDetail` in `src/components/RecipeManager.tsx`).
- Trigger `window.print()`.
- Add an `@media print` stylesheet (`src/index.css` is the only CSS file today; no print styles exist yet) that lays out a recipe cleanly for paper / PDF: title, meta (servings/times), ingredients, instructions. Hide app chrome (nav, buttons, toggles, delete/edit controls).
- 'Save as PDF' falls out for free via the browser print dialog — no separate export needed.

## Notes
- No print support of any kind exists in the app today (no window.print, no @media print, no print UI).
- Consider including the enhanced/emphasized instructions in the print output if they've been generated (see linked bead on enhanced-view offline resilience).

## Done when
- A recipe can be printed or saved to PDF from the detail view with a readable, app-chrome-free layout, with no live server dependency once the page is loaded.

title: Render recipe instructions as markdown (headers + lists), not raw text
description:
## Problem

Recipe `instructions` are authored/stored as markdown (a plain `String` — `recipe.instructions`, stored as `Text`), but the Recipe detail view renders the raw string with `whitespace-pre-wrap`, so structural markdown shows up literally:

- `## Caramelized Pineapple`, `## Macerated Cherries`, `## Custard Base` (sub-recipe component sections) render as literal `##` text instead of headers.
- `1. Melt 1 tbsp butter...` ordered steps render as literal `1.` prefixes instead of a styled list.

See the screenshot in the originating conversation — that raw-markdown output is exactly what we must NOT ship.

The existing **"Enhanced view"** toggle does NOT solve this: the `/recipes/{id}/enhance` endpoint (`server/src/services/recipe_enhancer.rs`) only injects ingredient amounts as `**bold**`, and the `EnhancedInstructions` component (`src/components/RecipeManager.tsx:771-815`) only parses inline `**bold**`. Neither path renders headers or lists.

## Goal

Render recipe instructions as proper markdown (at minimum: `##`/`###` headers, ordered + unordered lists, inline `**bold**`) in the Recipe detail view, so component sections and steps display as formatted content rather than raw markup.

## Two candidate approaches (decide during design)

- **A — Add a markdown renderer.** Install `react-markdown` (+ minimal plugins) and render the whole instructions string. Currently NO markdown lib is a dependency (only react / react-dom / react-router / tanstack-query), so this adds one. Cleanest fidelity; need to style headers/lists to match the design system and keep bundle impact reasonable.
- **B — Extend the existing hand-rolled parser.** Grow `EnhancedInstructions` / `renderInlineMarkdown` (CookingView.tsx:22-46) to handle `##` headers and `1.`/`-` lists in addition to `**bold**`. No new dependency, but reimplements markdown and risks drift / edge cases.

## Constraints / things not to break

- **Cook mode step segmentation.** `parseInstructionSteps()` (`src/types/recipe.ts:267-292`) splits instructions into discrete steps for `CookingView` by detecting numbered markers / blank lines, and strips the leading `1.`/`2)` markers. Cook mode (see [[fewd-cook-mode-ui-principles]], fewd-awo) NEEDS those discrete steps for step check-off / current-step highlight. A whole-string markdown renderer must coexist with step parsing — section headers (`##`) interleaved with a globally-numbered step list must not confuse the splitter (today the steps are numbered 1-8 across all three `##` sections).
- **Preserve enhanced-view ingredient bolding.** Whatever renders instructions must still render the `**amount ingredient**` spans the enhancer injects.
- **Design-system consistency.** Rendered headers/lists should use the app's typography tokens (Playfair headings / DM Sans body) and spacing, not browser defaults.
- Apply the same rendering in both the Recipe **detail view** and **cook mode** so the two stay visually consistent.

## Key files

- `src/components/RecipeManager.tsx` — `RecipeDetail` (instructions display ~1032-1046, "Enhanced view" toggle ~1010-1030), `EnhancedInstructions` (771-815)
- `src/components/CookingView.tsx` — `renderInlineMarkdown` (22-46), enhanced-step rendering (~118)
- `src/types/recipe.ts` — `parseInstructionSteps` (267-292), `Recipe.instructions` type (85)
- `server/src/services/recipe_enhancer.rs` — `enhance_instructions`
- `server/src/entities/recipe.rs` — `instructions` column (26)
acceptance_criteria: No literal markdown markers (##, 1., -) visible in the Recipe detail instructions view; section headers and numbered/bulleted steps render as formatted content; inline **bold** (enhanced-view ingredient amounts) still renders; cook-mode step check-off / parseInstructionSteps still segments steps correctly; rendered headings/lists use app typography tokens.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #58 (merge 5c6ea95). Renders recipe instructions + recipe/family notes as markdown via shared RecipeMarkdown (react-markdown, makeComponents factory, detail/cook/notes variants). Cook mode groups steps under ## headings via parseInstructionSections. Hardened parseInstructionSteps (contiguous-list split, decimal-safe + bullet-stripping markers). All gates green; verified in-app.

title: bd 1.0.4 export drops memories from issues.jsonl by default
description: bd 1.0.4 changed `bd export` to EXCLUDE `bd remember` memories by default (rationale: 'may contain sensitive agent context'; opt back in with --include-memories or --all). Consequence: any bare `bd export` or the auto-backup flow silently drops all memory rows from .beads/issues.jsonl, even though CLAUDE.md documents that file as carrying BOTH issue and memory rows. Without this, memories will keep getting re-dropped on the next auto-export.

description:

title: Add import_recipe_url MCP tool
description:
Add an MCP tool that imports a recipe from a public URL so Claude (or any MCP client) can save a recipe without the user manually pasting fields.

## Motivation

Feedback from a Claude session: "Recipe import by URL — No way to pull in a Caroline Chambers recipe directly from her site. You'd have to paste it manually. An import_recipe_url tool would be big for Amanda's favorites."

Today the MCP surface exposes 'create_recipe' (handler.rs) but every field has to be supplied by the model. For recipes that live on the web (Caroline Chambers, NYT Cooking, Smitten Kitchen, etc.) the LLM ends up doing fragile copy-paste of ingredients and steps. A dedicated import tool can:
- Fetch the page server-side
- Extract structured data (schema.org/Recipe JSON-LD is the dominant format; HTML fallback for sites that don't ship it)
- Normalize ingredients through the existing migration::ingredient_splitter / ingredient_amount helpers so amounts/units match the rest of the DB
- Return a populated CreateRecipeInput-shape that the LLM (or the tool itself) can persist via the existing service layer

## Scope (sketch — refine during design)

- New tool 'import_recipe_url' in server/src/mcp/handler.rs + schema in server/src/mcp/schemas/recipes.rs
- Backend fetch path: outbound HTTP client (reqwest) with timeout + size limit + allow only http/https + SSRF guards (no localhost / private IP ranges)
- Parser: prefer JSON-LD (@type Recipe / @graph), fall back to microdata / hRecipe; lean on an existing crate if one fits (e.g. recipe-scrapers parity in Rust is sparse — may need a small bespoke parser)
- Reuse migration::ingredient_splitter for ingredient text → (amount, unit, name, notes)
- Decide: does the tool persist directly (mirrors create_recipe) or return a draft for the LLM to confirm? Probably persist by default with a 'dry_run' flag, matching MCP design principle 'do the right thing by default server-side' (see 'bd memories fewd-mcp-design-principles')
- Surface unknown/unparseable fields as actionable errors per MCP error conventions in mcp/schemas/errors.rs
- Tests: unit tests against canned HTML fixtures (Caroline Chambers, NYT, AllRecipes), one integration test through the full MCP transport

## Open questions

- Auth/rate limits on the outbound fetch? Probably fine with a per-call timeout + UA string; revisit if abuse surfaces
- How to handle paywalled sites that gate JSON-LD behind auth — error cleanly with a suggestion to paste manually
- Image import: download + store, or just record source URL? Likely just URL for v1 to keep storage simple

## References

- Existing MCP tool surface: server/src/mcp/handler.rs (create_recipe is the closest sibling)
- Ingredient parsing helpers: migration::ingredient_splitter, migration::ingredient_amount
- MCP design principles: bd memories fewd-mcp-design-principles
- Curated recipe entity: server/src/entities/curated_recipe.rs

title: Scale Recipe form: 3-column display with Ratio reference + free-form editing
description:
Replace the post-Preview state of the Scale Recipe form with a simpler design that matches how kitchens actually scale recipes (round and accept small drift, rather than hunt for mathematically clean multipliers).

Full design in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-17-recipe-scaling-rebalance-and-fine-tune-design.md (revised 2026-05-17 after chef-domain reality check — earlier draft proposed a clean-multiplier-hunting Rebalance machinery that was over-engineered for the actual domain).

Summary of changes:
- Three-column ingredient row: Original | Current (editable, every row) | Ratio vs. original.
- Every row's Current is editable as a free-form input. Edits are local — no cascading, no Rebalance button, no clean-multiplier search.
- Ratio column shows current/original per-ingredient as a sanity check and fine-tune reference. Has no gating power.
- Save labels stay simple ('Save as New Recipe' / 'Update This Recipe').
- Remove the flagged-row highlight machinery and warning banner (subject to ordering with fewd-2bp — see spec).

Implementation scope (frontend-only):
- Rewrite the ingredient list section in RecipeManager.tsx (Scale Recipe panel) to a 3-column grid.
- Every row gets an editable Current input wired through existing handleIngredientChange.
- Add Ratio column rendering current/original formatted as e.g. '1.67x'.
- Remove flagged-highlight + warning banner per the spec's ordering rules.

No backend changes. No DB migration, no new HTTP route, no schema change.

Related: fewd-2bp (auto-round at Preview — composable, should ship first), fewd-0mt (highlight bug, closed by this work), fewd-bhd (weight-based scaling — potential future pivot), fewd-p3j (shopping-list rounding, different service).

title: Recipe scaler: auto-round discrete units (eggs, cloves, etc.) to whole integers
description:
The Scale Recipe form scales discrete-unit ingredients to fractional values (e.g. 3.75 eggs at 4→5 servings) and asks the user to manually fix them via the 'fractional' input UI. The user shouldn't have to do this — there's no such thing as 3.75 eggs in a kitchen.

Mirror the rounding intent from fewd-p3j (which targets the shopping-list aggregator) into the interactive recipe scaler at server/src/services/recipe_scaler.rs. The fix is localized to that one service — the shopping aggregator stays unrounded as designed.

Design notes:
- Today, recipe_scaler.rs detects discrete units via is_discrete_unit (unit not weight/volume) and rounds to 2 decimals. It then flags any non-integer result.
- New behavior: when is_discrete_unit is true, round the scaled value to a whole integer. Recommend nearest-integer (round half away from zero) for cooking context — ceil-only would over-buy ingredients you already measured. For ranges, round both min and max.
- Keep the FlaggedIngredient + manual-adjust UI for cases where the user wants a different value than the round picked (e.g. 0.5→1 rounded but cook wants 0.5 for a smaller variant). The flag would now indicate 'we auto-rounded, here's the editable value' rather than 'broken state, please fix'. Update the banner copy in RecipeManager.tsx accordingly.
- scale_one (recursive for or_alternative chains) currently does NOT flag; preserve that scoping — auto-round primaries only by default, or audit whether alt chains should round too (probably yes for cooking consistency, but verify against the 'one ingredient slot' UX comment at recipe_scaler.rs:42-46).

Acceptance: scaling a recipe from 4→5 servings on a 3-egg recipe yields 4 eggs (not 3.75), no manual fix required. Tests cover discrete units, ranges, and or_alternative chains. The 'fractional' UI still appears but as an override path rather than a required fix-up.

title: Recipes tab: client-side sort dropdown (name / rating / last-made / times-made / created)
description:
The Recipes tab today has substring search by name only (`RecipeManager.tsx`
line 1113-1115); recipes render in server-determined Name-ASC order with
no UI control over ordering. At ~24 recipes the lack-of-sort is annoying,
at 50+ it makes finding the right recipe a real chore. Sort is the
smallest UX cut that delivers immediate value — strictly orthogonal to
the larger filter-panel work tracked in fewd-pz8.

## What to add

A sort selector above the recipe grid (next to the existing search input
on `RecipeManager.tsx` line 1244-1254). Options:

| Label                       | Field         | Direction | NULL placement       |
| --------------------------- | ------------- | --------- | -------------------- |
| Name (A–Z)  *(default)*     | `name`        | ASC       | (no nulls)           |
| Name (Z–A)                  | `name`        | DESC      | (no nulls)           |
| Highest rated               | `rating`      | DESC      | NULLs last           |
| Most-made                   | `times_made`  | DESC      | (0 sorts last)       |
| Recently made               | `last_made`   | DESC      | NULLs last           |
| Not made in a while         | `last_made`   | ASC       | NULLs FIRST (never-made bubbles up) |
| Newly added                 | `created_at`  | DESC      | (no nulls)           |
| Favorites first             | `is_favorite` | DESC, then `name` ASC tiebreaker | n/a |

Implementation: client-side sort over the existing `useRecipes()` result.
The data's already in memory; no backend changes needed at current scale.
At 100+ recipes per fewd-0a9's projection, server-side becomes useful —
but that's a future swap, not a blocker.

## State persistence

Default `name-asc`. Persist user's last selection in `localStorage` keyed
on something like `fewd.recipes.sortBy` so reload/return keeps the order
they chose. URL query-string also acceptable — pick during build based on
whether shareable links matter (probably not for this surface).

## NULL handling

`last_made` and `rating` are nullable. Document the rule in the comparator
(JS sort is not stable for NaN/undefined the way you'd hope):

- Sort DESC by rating: NULLs go last
- Sort ASC by last_made (the 'haven't made in a while' use case): NULLs go FIRST so
  never-cooked recipes surface for cooking. This is the SAME policy as
  `RecipeSortField::LastMade` ASC in fewd-0a9 for consistency.

Pin this rule in tests.

## Tests

- Component test: change the sort dropdown, verify the rendered card order
  reflects the new ordering for at least 'name-asc', 'rating-desc',
  'last_made-asc' (the never-made-bubble-up case).
- Component test: NULL handling — recipe with `rating: null` sorts last
  on rating-desc, but appears wherever expected on name-asc.
- Tie-breaker: when two recipes have identical sort-key value (same
  rating, same last_made), fall back to `name` ASC so the order doesn't
  shimmer between renders.
- localStorage round-trip: pick rating-desc, reload, sort still rating-desc.

## NOT in scope

- Server-side sort. `GET /api/recipes` keeps its current Name-ASC default.
  Client-side is sufficient at this scale.
- Filter chips (tags, persona dislikes, time, favorites-only) — that's
  fewd-pz8's lane. Sort and filter are orthogonal; this bead handles only
  the reorder.
- Sort UI in the MealPlanner recipe picker (fewd-vej's combobox lives
  there and has its own UX considerations).
- Curated view toggle (also fewd-pz8). The sort dropdown only applies to
  the 'all recipes' view; if/when the curated view ships it can opt-out
  of sort (curated is policy-determined ordering).

## Why P2 not P3

User asked for it after a real session where finding a recipe was hard.
Trivially scoped (one component, one new dropdown, client-side sort). Low
risk, high daily ROI, fast to ship.

## References

- fewd-0a9 — MCP backend sort_by (open). Field list above mirrors 0a9's
  enum so the two stay consistent if/when this swaps to server-side.
- fewd-pz8 — Recipes-tab filter panel + curated view toggle (open). Sister
  bead in UX terms but independently shippable.
- `src/components/RecipeManager.tsx:1100-1267` — current shape; sort
  dropdown slots in alongside the search input.
- `src/hooks/useRecipes.ts` — returns full list; no changes needed here.
- `server/src/services/recipe_service.rs:56` — current Name-ASC server
  default. Leave it alone for this bead.

title: search_recipes: includes_ingredient_substrings filter (find recipes that contain ingredient X)
description:
Today the MCP `search_recipes` tool lets the LLM EXCLUDE recipes by ingredient
(`excluded_ingredient_substrings`, fewd-0kk), but there's no inclusive
counterpart. Asking 'show me all recipes that contain spam' forces the LLM
to either pull every recipe via `list_curated_recipes` + paginate the rest
(can't — full archive is intentionally not exposed) or to call
`search_recipes` with some other filter and post-filter in-conversation.
Real session 2026-05-11: the user asked an MCP client this exact question
and the client had to walk every recipe.

This is the symmetric twin of the already-shipped exclude filter and shares
all the underlying machinery.

## What to add

A new filter on `search_recipes`:

    includes_ingredient_substrings: Vec<String>

Semantics: a recipe matches when EVERY substring in the list appears in
SOME ingredient's `name` (case-insensitive substring match). Multiple
substrings AND together — `["spam", "cheese"]` means "recipes with both
spam AND cheese," not "either." This matches how the exclude filter
composes (every excluded substring must be absent), so the two are
mirror-images in semantics as well as in implementation.

## Implementation

`server/src/services/recipe_service.rs::search_filtered` already has the
EXISTS-over-`json_each` + `json_extract(ie.value, '$.name')` + `instr()`
pattern for the exclude case (lines 354-368). Drop the `NOT` and append
one EXISTS clause per included substring. Pushes into the SeaORM query
so it scales with catalog size — matches the project's filter-at-DB rule.

Wire-up checklist:
1. `SearchFilters` gets `included_ingredient_substrings: Vec<String>`.
2. `search_filtered` appends `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(...) ... instr(LOWER(name), ?) > 0)` per substring.
3. `SearchRecipesParams` (in `server/src/mcp/schemas/recipes.rs` — wherever the exclude param lives) gets the matching field + tool-input plumbing.
4. `SearchRecipesParams::validate_has_filter` counts it as a non-trivial filter so a bare call with only this param still passes.
5. `is_empty()` on `SearchFilters` returns false when this vec is non-empty.

## Tool description (starting point, not final)

> Use BEFORE `create_recipe` when the user names an ingredient they want
> to use ('what can I make with spam?', 'recipes that use leftover
> rice'). Composes with every other filter — combine with `tags=["dinner"]`
> for 'dinner recipes that use spam.' Case-insensitive substring match
> against ingredient names; 'olive' matches 'olive oil' and 'pitted olives'
> alike. Multiple values AND together.

## Substring-match notes (less dangerous than excludes)

For exclude: false positives HIDE recipes the user might want
('olive' disliked → 'olive oil' recipes vanish). Documented caveat in
fewd-0kk's exclude path.

For include: false positives SURFACE extra hits the user mentally
filters ('spam' → matches a recipe with a 'spamoosa' tag if one
existed). Lower-stakes failure mode. No additional documentation burden.

## Tests

- `search_filtered` test: single-substring match returns the right recipes,
  excludes the rest.
- `search_filtered` test: multi-substring AND semantics (returns only
  recipes with BOTH ingredients).
- `search_filtered` test: empty Vec is a no-op (treated as 'no filter on
  this axis').
- `search_filtered` test: combining include + exclude on the same substring
  ('include spam, exclude tofu') works without contradiction.
- MCP-level test: `validate_has_filter` accepts a call with only
  `includes_ingredient_substrings` set.
- Calibration test: at least one fixture recipe contains 'spam' in some
  ingredient, the search returns it.

## UI follow-up (separate from this bead's MCP scope)

The user explicitly wants this in the UI too. Two existing beads are the
natural homes — leave the call until this MCP work lands:

- **fewd-pz8** (Recipes-tab filter panel) — already lists tags / time / rating /
  favorites / persona-dislikes as filter chips. Adding an
  'contains ingredient...' input fits the same panel. When fewd-pz8 is
  picked up, expand its scope to include this filter chip, OR file a small
  ride-along bead.
- **fewd-vej** (MealPlanner combobox) — a recipe picker that supports
  'show me recipes that contain X' as a search modifier is one possible
  shape, but secondary to the primary 'find by recipe name' goal of vej.
  Probably out of scope there.

Surface this in whichever filter-panel bead is in-flight when the UI work
happens.

## Why P2 not P3

The exclude filter is already P2-equivalent (shipped in fewd-0kk).
Inclusive search is the harder gap to work around — exclude can be
emulated by 'don't pick those' in conversation, but include requires
walking the whole archive without this filter. Real-session evidence
above.

## References

- fewd-0kk — sibling exclude filter (closed). Same SeaORM pattern, same
  param-validation shape.
- fewd-2mk — favorites-based ranking. Different concern (rank vs filter)
  but the design discussion of 'how do multiple persons combine' rhymes
  with the AND semantics chosen here.
- `server/src/services/recipe_service.rs:354-368` — exact JSON-traversal
  precedent.
- `bd memories fewd-mcp-design-principles` — error-on-unknown,
  actionable-message conventions apply here too (substring that matches
  zero ingredients in the catalog should not error — it's a valid 'no
  results' answer — but a malformed input WOULD error per the principles).

title: Rewrite MCP tool descriptions to lead with task intent (improve tool_search ranking)
description:
Claude Desktop (and probably other MCP clients) selects tools via embedding-similarity tool_search, returning a top-K subset rather than loading the full catalog. In a real meal-planning session, `list_meals` and `get_shopping_list` failed to rank into the top-5 — Claude planned the entire week without ever checking existing schedule or generating the shopping list, because those tools were effectively invisible to it.

Diagnosis: the descriptions of those tools lead with output mechanics ('Returns meals across a date range...', 'Generate a consolidated grocery list with unit conversion...') rather than task intent ('Check what's already scheduled before scheduling more'). The tools that DID rank (`search_recipes`, `create_meal`, `list_curated_recipes`, etc.) all have intent verbs in slot 1.

This is a discoverability bug masquerading as a documentation problem.

## What needs to be done

Rewrite every MCP tool description in server/src/mcp/handler.rs to follow this pattern:

1. **Sentence 1**: when/why to use it (task intent, with workflow positioning when applicable — 'BEFORE create_meal,' 'AFTER planning,' 'when the user mentions...').
2. **Sentence 2**: what it does mechanically (current text, lightly trimmed).
3. **Sentence 3+ (optional)**: error semantics, cross-references to related tools.

## Tools to audit

All tools currently in handler.rs:

- `whoami` (handler.rs:57)
- `list_curated_recipes` (76) — already strong, light touch
- `search_recipes` (106) — already strong
- `get_recipe` (191) — already strong
- `list_people` (236)

## Concrete rewrites for the two confirmed failures (starting points, not final)

`list_meals`:
> Check what dinners (or other meal slots) are already scheduled — call BEFORE `create_meal` to avoid duplicates and to see prior-week patterns. Returns meals across an inclusive date range with assigned servings (who's eating what, how many servings, optional per-serving notes).

`get_shopping_list`:
> Produce the week's grocery list AFTER you've planned meals with `create_meal`. Aggregates ingredients across all scheduled meals in the date range, scaled by person-servings, with unit conversion where compatible. Each item carries per-meal sources so the user can trace 'why is there extra flour?' back to the contributing recipes.

- Don't break existing input-schema contracts. This is a description-only change; no input/output shape changes.

title: Add update_person MCP tool
description:
Add an `update_person` tool so the LLM can write to per-person preference fields. Today the MCP surface is read-only for people (`list_people`, `get_family_overview`) — every preference learned during a session ('Cleo: pull from oven before glazing') has to live in Claude's session memory and re-emerge from scratch each conversation. fewd's Person entity already has the fields; we just need a write path.

## Writable fields (all from server/src/entities/person.rs)

- `notes: Option<String>` — free-form standing notes about the person (the gnocchi-session example: 'pull before glazing for kid #2')
- `dislikes: String` — comma-separated or however the existing schema stores them; mirror the read shape
- `favorites: String`
- `drink_preferences: Option<String>`
- `drink_dislikes: Option<String>`

NOT writable via this tool (separate concern, may want dedicated tools later):
- `name` — identity, frozen for the same reason recipe slugs are frozen (other tables reference it)
- `is_active` — soft-delete; deserves its own `deactivate_person` / `reactivate_person` tool with confirmation semantics
- birthdates, dietary-goal structured fields if any — file follow-ups if needed

## What needs to be done

1. **Schema** — add `UpdatePersonInput` to server/src/mcp/schemas/people.rs. Identify by `name` (case-insensitive, consistent with how `list_people` and `create_meal` resolve people). Every field optional for PATCH semantics. Decide explicit-clear semantics: `Option<Option<String>>` with null for the `Option<String>` fields, or paired `clear_notes: bool` flags. Match whatever decision lands on fewd-s6q for consistency across the MCP surface.
2. **Tool method** — `async fn update_person` in server/src/mcp/handler.rs.
3. **Service** — check whether `PersonService` at server/src/services/person_service.rs has an `update` method already (the HTTP routes write these fields, so likely yes). Reuse it; add a partial-update DTO if needed.
4. **Error handling** — unknown name returns the standard actionable error pointing at `list_people` (precedent: search_recipes' `excludes_for_persons` error path at handler.rs around line 145).
5. **Authorization consideration** — should any family member be able to update *any other* family member's notes? The current threat model is 'any authed user is admin' (per `bd memories fewd-mcp-design-principles` and the release-readiness epic fewd-2y6 docs), so for now: yes, no per-person restriction. Document this in the tool description so it isn't accidentally tightened later without thought. After the opaque-token migration (fewd-2y6.6) lands, this could be revisited.
6. **Cross-references** — mention `update_person` in `get_family_overview`, `list_people`, and the top-level `instructions` block. The natural workflow surface: the LLM learns something about a family member during a conversation → writes it via `update_person` so future sessions inherit it.

## Open questions

- Should `notes` be a single string field (current schema) or a list of dated entries? Single string is what exists; list-of-entries is more LLM-friendly long-term but is a schema migration. File as a follow-up if the single-string version turns out to drift into a stale-string problem.

title: Add get_meal_planner_printable MCP tool
description:
Add an MCP tool that generates a printable meal-planner output from scheduled meals. Standardizes the 'fridge card' format Steve has been having Claude generate week-to-week, so it's reproducible without relying on Claude's session memory or prompt phrasing.

Claude has converged on a layout that works well for this household; the goal is to capture that layout server-side as the canonical version and have the tool emit it deterministically.

## What needs to be done

1. **Capture the canonical layout.** Before implementing, ask Steve to paste a recent printable Claude generated that he liked. That's the design target. Document it in the bead notes. Likely shape: per-day section headers (Mon/Tue/...) with meal-slot bullets, but treat the captured example as authoritative.
2. **Schema** (server/src/mcp/schemas/meals.rs or new schemas/printable.rs):
   - `PrintableInput {`
     - `start_date: NaiveDate` (required)
     - `end_date: NaiveDate` (required, capped at 14 days span — this is for fridge use, not a quarterly meal plan)
     - `include: Vec<MealSlot>` (default: [Dinner], options: Breakfast/Lunch/Dinner/Snack — multi-select)
     - `format: PrintableFormat` (default: Markdown; future: PlainText, possibly SimpleHtml)
     - `show_servings: bool` (default: true — useful for split-cooking households)
     - `show_assignees: bool` (default: false — fridge cards usually don't need 'Steve eats X, Amanda eats Y')
   - `}`
3. **Tool method** `async fn get_meal_planner_printable` in server/src/mcp/handler.rs. Loads meals via `MealService::get_all_for_date_range` (already used by `list_meals`), formats per the canonical layout, returns the rendered string.
4. **Cross-references.** Mention this tool in the top-level `instructions` block as the 'finishing step' after planning the week. Add reference from `list_meals` description: 'use `get_meal_planner_printable` for a fridge-ready output.'
5. **Tests.** Snapshot-test the rendered output for a fixture week. Also test: empty week (no meals scheduled) returns a coherent message rather than an empty card; date-range cap rejection; meal-slot filter (Dinner-only vs. all four).

## Why a tool, not a resource

Resource URIs in MCP don't carry parameters cleanly (URI templates exist but aren't widely supported). This output is fundamentally parameterized (date range, meal-slot filter, format), so a tool is the right primitive. Claude Desktop renders the returned markdown inline; the user prints from there.

## Open questions

- Layout rendering: pure markdown, or escape into a small templating helper? Markdown is fine for v1; if the layout grows complex (icons, color hints, ingredient teasers) revisit.
- 'Predictability' is the explicit goal — should the rendered output also include a small footer like `Generated 2026-05-10 | Mon-Sun, dinners only` so a user comparing two printables can see what differs? Probably yes.
- Should this tool itself be exposed as a *prompt* too (the LLM might prefer to call a prompt that wraps it)? Probably not — the prompt would just be 'call get_meal_planner_printable with these args' which the LLM can do directly. Tools first, add a prompt only if a wrapper workflow emerges.

## References

- Meal loading: server/src/services/meal_service.rs (`get_all_for_date_range`)
- Existing tool that uses date range params: server/src/mcp/handler.rs:296 (`list_meals`)
- Date-range cap helper: same file (look for the 14-day cap pattern from fewd-2y6.5)
- Related: fewd-2y6 (release readiness — this is a follow-up feature, not release-gating)

Layout merges may11 reference (vertical day-row list, Amandas preference) with may4 styling (cream-yellow background, italic terracotta titles, Playfair Display + Inter, Steves preference). Canonical template lives at server/src/services/printable/template.html. v1 takes overlay annotations from the LLM (week_theme, use_up_notes, dont_forget, day_overlays, foot_note) rather than persisting them. Date range capped at 14 inclusive days (PrintableSpanTooWide). Multi-recipe meals render primary + "Also: {others}". Per-person color theming deferred (neutral pills v1). Single-page-letter fit verified in print-media emulation: 855px tall vs 979px usable (124px headroom). title: Add weekly_dinner_plan MCP prompt
description:
Add MCP prompts support to the fewd server, starting with a `weekly_dinner_plan` prompt that captures the standard week-planning workflow Steve has been pasting into Claude Desktop manually.

Claude Desktop supports MCP prompts (`prompts/list` + `prompts/get` from the spec) — they surface as selectable slash-command-style entries. Server-side prompts are the right place for household-canonical workflows so all family members get the same version.

## What needs to be done

1. **Wire up rmcp prompts capability.** Add the `prompts` capability to the `ServerHandler` impl in server/src/mcp/handler.rs, including `list_prompts` and `get_prompt` methods. Confirm rmcp's prompt traits — likely a `#[prompt]` attribute analogous to `#[tool]`. If rmcp's prompt support is missing/limited, document the workaround.
2. **Add module structure.** Mirror the tool layout: server/src/mcp/prompts/ with one file per prompt, schemas/prompts.rs for prompt argument types.
3. **Implement `weekly_dinner_plan`.** Inputs:
   - `week_start_date: NaiveDate` (required, must be a Monday — validate)
   - `family_schedule: String` (required, free-form prose — typically several sentences describing the week's activities, who's home when, dietary considerations for the week, etc. NOT structured; the LLM is good at parsing prose).
   - `who_is_planning: Option<String>` — defaults to the authenticated person; explicit override for 'plan as if I'm Amanda this week.'
   Returns a prompt string that:
   - Sets up the LLM to plan dinners for week_start_date through week_start_date+6
   - Embeds family_schedule verbatim so the LLM sees the human's context
   - Tells the LLM the canonical workflow: get_family_overview → search_recipes (with prefer_for_persons or favorites bias) → list_meals (check existing scheduled) → create_meal per day → get_shopping_list at end
   - Reminds the LLM to call mark_recipe_made for any past meals the user mentions in family_schedule (after fewd-i8e ships)
4. **Test the rendered prompt.** A test should snapshot-compare the rendered prompt for representative inputs so accidental drift in the canonical workflow is caught in CI.

## Open questions

- Should the prompt be parameterized by family member, or always plan-for-everyone? The `who_is_planning` arg above splits the difference.
- Is there a way to make the prompt include a fresh-each-time embedding of `get_family_overview` so the LLM doesn't need to re-fetch? Probably no — prompts are static strings, but the prompt body can instruct the LLM to fetch the resource as step 1, which is fine.
- After this works for weekly planning, what other prompts make sense? `make_shopping_list_for_week`, `recipe_audit` (Amanda's prep-time concern from the conversation), `adapt_for_dietary_change`...

## References

- Existing tool wiring pattern: server/src/mcp/handler.rs (each #[tool])

This is the highest-leverage MCP addition for actual household use: it converts a recurring manual paste into a discoverable, version-controlled workflow that gets better as fewd's tool surface grows.

title: Add adapt_recipe MCP tool (LLM-driven variant creation)
description:
Expose the existing 'adapt recipe' affordance to MCP, but inverted: the caller (Claude) IS the LLM, so the tool persists the adaptation rather than generating it. Solves the gnocchi-with-different-sausage case from the meal planning session — creating a one-off variant instead of editing the original or stuffing the change into a serving note.

## Why a separate tool from update_recipe (fewd-s6q)

`update_recipe` mutates the original. `adapt_recipe` creates a new recipe row linked to its parent — so the family's regular gnocchi recipe stays clean while still capturing 'we made it with hot Italian sausage that one Tuesday.'

The Recipe entity already has a `parent_recipe_id` foreign key for exactly this purpose. The HTTP/UI 'adapt' flow uses an LLM to synthesize the variant; the MCP version skips that round trip because Claude is already generating the changes.

## Open design questions (decide during bead planning)

1. **Variant vs. ad-hoc serving.** Two valid shapes:
   - (a) Persist as a child Recipe row with `parent_recipe_id` set. Searchable, ratable, can be made again. Adds a recipe to the catalog.
   - (b) Persist on the MealServing as enriched adaptation metadata (changed_ingredients, changed_instructions), not a Recipe row. Doesn't pollute search results with one-offs.
   - Hybrid: `save_as_variant: bool` parameter — false = ad-hoc serving enrichment, true = persisted child Recipe. Most flexible; matches how a human thinks ('try this once' vs. 'this is now my version').

2. **Tool inputs.** Probably:
   - `parent_slug: String` (required, must exist)
   - `name: Option<String>` (defaults to '$parent_name (variant)' or similar — server picks if omitted)
   - `ingredient_changes: Vec<IngredientChange>` where IngredientChange is { add | replace { old, new } | remove } so the LLM doesn't need to re-send the full ingredient list (huge token savings)
   - `instruction_changes: Vec<InstructionChange>` similar
   - `notes: Option<String>` — free-form 'why this variant exists'
   - `save_as_variant: bool` (per option 1 above)

3. **HTTP/UI rework.** Today the UI calls /api/recipes/adapt which invokes a server-side LLM. After this lands, the UI's adapt flow could optionally accept pre-generated changes (when caller is itself an LLM-driven flow) and skip the LLM call. That's a separate beads issue — file a child once shape is locked.

## References

- Existing parent linkage: `parent_recipe_id` field on recipe entity
- HTTP adapt route: server/src/routes/recipes.rs (LLM-driven adapt endpoint)
- Frontend adapt: src/components/AdaptRecipePanel.tsx
- Related design principle: `bd memories fewd-mcp-design-principles` ('respect the domain model's expressiveness at the boundary rather than flattening it')
- Related: fewd-s6q (update_recipe — kept structural-only; this tool handles the variant case)

## Out of scope

- Reworking the UI adapt feature to skip the LLM call when given pre-generated changes (file as child after MCP shape is locked).

title: Add mark_recipe_made MCP tool
description:
Add a dedicated `mark_recipe_made` tool to the MCP server. Carved out of fewd-s6q (`update_recipe`) for the narrower "we cooked this tonight" intent. This is the most valuable of the three split-out tools because it's the natural conversational follow-up to a meal plan: "we made the chili last night" → LLM marks it made.

1. **New service helper required** — unlike favorite/rating, `times_made` and `last_made` have NO dedicated service method today. `RecipeService` at server/src/services/recipe_service.rs initializes both at create time (`times_made: Set(0)`, `last_made: Set(None)` at lines 121-122) but the generic `update` path doesn't handle them. Add `RecipeService::mark_made(db, id, on_date: Option<NaiveDate>)` that:
   - Increments `times_made` by 1
   - Sets `last_made` to `on_date.unwrap_or_else(today)`
   - Returns the updated model
   Do this in a transaction so concurrent calls don't race the increment.
2. **Schema** — add `MarkRecipeMadeInput { slug: String, on_date: Option<NaiveDate> }` to server/src/mcp/schemas/recipes.rs. Default `on_date` to today server-side (per the design principle "do the right thing by default server-side"). Document YYYY-MM-DD format consistent with the rest of the MCP date inputs.
